scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Users on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) report they cannot
reach each other in either direction. Both hosts can still ping their
own gateways (10.0.0.1 and 10.0.1.1). The NOC insists the fabric is
healthy: every BGP session is Established, all routes are present on
every router, no interface has flapped, and all FRR daemons are
running. Identify what is silently eating the traffic.

injection.action: add a FORWARD DROP rule for pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 transit

post_inject_check.expect: 0% loss   (gateway still OK -- INPUT chain untouched)

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: leaf_router_0_0 iptables FORWARD chain
Mechanism: a DROP rule on leaf_router_0_0 discards every forwarded
  packet with source in 10.0.0.0/24 and destination in 10.0.1.0/24.
  All pc_0_0 traffic must transit leaf_router_0_0 (its only gateway),
  so pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 packets die there. The reverse direction fails
  too, despite matching no rule on its way in: pc_0_1's echo requests
  ARE delivered to pc_0_0, but pc_0_0's replies (src 10.0.0.2, dst
  10.0.1.2) match the rule and are dropped -- a one-directional filter
  breaks bidirectional traffic. Routing and BGP are completely
  healthy; the drop is at the firewall layer. Local delivery to the
  gateway itself uses the INPUT chain, which is untouched, so both
  hosts still ping their gateways.
Localization: leaf_router_0_0
Root cause: extraneous iptables FORWARD DROP rule
  (-s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24) on leaf_router_0_0
Fix: `iptables -D FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24 -j DROP` on
  leaf_router_0_0
scenario.fix_spec:
remove the DROP rule on leaf_router_0_0 --
`iptables -D FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24 -j DROP`
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: iptables FORWARD DROP / firewall filter
must-recognize-filter-pattern: recognizes healthy routing + healthy BGP with silent forwarding loss as a packet-filter fault, not a routing fault
bonus-explains-asymmetric-drop: explains that the single directional rule (10.0.0.0/24 -> 10.0.1.0/24) also kills the reverse ping because replies match it

agent.diagnosis_text:
A rogue iptables rule in the Linux netfilter FORWARD chain on
leaf_router_0_0 is silently dropping all transit traffic between the
two host subnets. The rule — `DROP all -- * * 10.0.0.0/24
10.0.1.0/24` — is installed at position 1 of the FORWARD chain and
had already matched 6 packets (504 bytes) at the time of inspection.
No other device in the fabric (leaf_router_0_1, spine_router_0_0,
spine_router_0_1, super_spine_router_0) carries any FORWARD-chain
rules; all are clean.

This single asymmetric rule explains both failure directions. When
pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) sends traffic toward pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2), the packet
is forwarded through leaf_router_0_0, immediately matches the DROP
rule (src ∈ 10.0.0.0/24, dst ∈ 10.0.1.0/24), and is silently
discarded — the ICMP request never reaches the spine. In the reverse
direction, pc_0_1's request can reach pc_0_0 (it traverses
leaf_router_0_1, which is clean, then arrives at leaf_router_0_0 with
src=10.0.1.x which does not match the rule), but pc_0_0's reply
(src=10.0.0.2, dst=10.0.1.2) exits through leaf_router_0_0's FORWARD
chain and is dropped by the same rule. Gateway pings succeed because
those packets are local (INPUT/OUTPUT path, not forwarded), so
netfilter's FORWARD chain is never traversed.

The FRR/BGP control plane is entirely healthy — routes, sessions, and
daemons are all correct — which is why the NOC's routing-level
observability showed nothing; the fault lives entirely in the kernel's
netfilter layer, below FRR's visibility.

Root cause: a `DROP` rule injected into the iptables FORWARD chain on
leaf_router_0_0 blocks all inter-subnet forwarded traffic sourced from
10.0.0.0/24 destined to 10.0.1.0/24, making both host-to-host
directions fail.

Corrective fix: on leaf_router_0_0, run
`iptables -D FORWARD -s 10.0.0.0/24 -d 10.0.1.0/24 -j DROP`
to remove the rule, then verify with `iptables -L FORWARD -n -v` that
the chain is empty and confirm end-to-end ping between pc_0_0 and
pc_0_1 restores successfully.
